"to make room for new spans" reads as trimming a cache, but eviction is stronger than that:
`evictOldestLocked` does `entry.state.Store(true)`, so a span that is still in flight gets
treated as ended by every goroutine holding it, and spans started under it stop being linked to
it as parent. That is exactly the user-visible symptom this PR describes ("some spans get the
wrong parent under load"), so it's the one detail an operator needs in order to recognize the
condition. The code comment on `defaultMaxSpanStates` already says it plainly; the user-facing
docs don't. Unlike `OTEL_GLS_MAX_SPANS` above, this knob also has no guidance on when to raise it.

```suggestion
- `OTEL_GLS_MAX_SPAN_STATES` (default `100000`) bounds the shared span lifecycle map used across
  all goroutines to recognize when a span has ended. Once it is full, the oldest tracked entry is
  evicted (also logged at debug level) to make room for new spans. Eviction marks that entry
  ended, so a span still in flight loses implicit propagation and spans started under it are no
  longer linked to it as parent. Raise the limit if a workload keeps more spans concurrently in
  flight than the default allows.
```

That's intentional and matches `InstFileRule`/`InstFuncRule`. One consequence: if a rule author's own JSON (rather than YAML) input ever included a `resolved_path` key, it would be silently honored instead of being computed by setup. Worth confirming that JSON is never an accepted user-facing input format for rules, or explicitly ignoring the field on read.

Helper output files are named `otelc.<ruleName>.<helperFileBase>.go` — the rule name is baked into the filename. If two distinct call rules both reference a helper file that lives in the same source path (e.g. two rules pointing at the same `path:` directory and both needing `Wrapper`), each rule materializes its own copy of that file into the target package under a different generated name, and the target package ends up with `Wrapper` declared twice — a compile-time redeclaration error.

File rules avoid this because their output name (`apply_file.go`'s `otelc.<fileBase>.go`) has no rule prefix, so `!util.PathExists(newFile)` naturally dedups repeat references to the same file. Call rules don't get that dedup here since the name varies per rule.

Is sharing one helper file across multiple call rules a supported scenario? If so, this needs either a rule-independent output name (with a correctness argument for why that's safe) or an explicit dedup/collision check.

reason phrase) doesn't fully cover the fix: it can't distinguish "we always
strip the code correctly" from "we happened to match this one status line."
